column1: # What explains a step in a benchmark row's drift since the anchor, for the weekly chart of
# unexplained drift on `main` (helpers/baseline_drift.py; calef's ruling on #2554, 2026-10-22 UTC).
# A step is one floor save's move on a row, or `main`'s gap to the current floor. A step no line
# explains is unexplained, and above 5% that is a lane to open. Name: provisional, minted
# One line per claim, five tab-separated fields: arch, commit, row, percent, cause.
# - percent `*` claims the whole step of the save `commit` names: its own code change, or one term
#   measured alone (the compiler, the emulator). Only a save can carry `*`; script/metrics refuses
# - a number claims that much of whichever step's range holds `commit` (a merge, or a commit
#   inside one), compounded with the others. Write it against the merge's parent, as measured.
# - row `*` is every row the save moved.
# - a save that "absorbs drift already on main" or "mixes the compiler with drift on main" gets no
#   line for that part; "partly" with no number gets none either. A split nobody measured is not
# A `--save` that accounts for its moves adds its lines here in the same pull request; the
# baseline file cannot hold them, because a save rebuilds it (script/bench's BUGS). An attribution
# found later, a bisect in a note for instance, is transcribed here with its numbers.
# The records the causes below cite: milestone 23 (a capability-routed component OS with live
# replacement), milestone 58 (RISC-V TLB shootdown), milestone 124 (a thread is born where it
# lives), milestone 126 (the `procps` package), milestone 139 (drive the unsafe count down),
# milestone 142 (a text display good enough that people use it), milestone 206 (a program image
# has under 896 KiB), milestone 299 (the x86 port-range capability), milestone 300 (decompose the
# icount baseline drift), milestone 447 (a thread's vector registers are its own), milestone 541
# (a timed window that excludes preemption), milestone 629 (the context-switch statistic stops
# costing the switch path), milestone 812 (`std::thread::spawn` runs real threads in one address
# space), §204 (how userspace asks where a thread runs).
# The pre-ledger saves (before 2026-09-23), read as explained by the change their own commit
# names. EXCEPTION, marked, by calef's ruling on #2554 (2026-10-22 UTC): these saves also
# absorbed drift on main that nothing separated, and nothing can separate it now.
